correctness.rationale: For all a>b>0 and even B>=2, direct Lanczos orthogonality makes two nodes exact and the one-node estimator equal to ||g||^4/(g^T A g). Independent chi-square radial moments E R²=2 and E R⁴=8 and exact angular integrals 1/sqrt(ab), (a+b)/(2(ab)^(3/2)) determine its bias and variance. Deep Gaussian quadratic-form variance is 2 tr(A^-2). Symbolic simplification gives the displayed MSEs and difference. The B-star derivative is strictly negative for every u>1 because 3u²-4u+3>0, with limits infinity and four, proving the iff classification. The embedded verifier replayed these symbolic identities, three rational Krylov certificates and numerical diagnostics. Experiments are supplemental and no repeated-eigenvalue or floating-point claim is made.

value.rationale: The tension between number of independent Monte Carlo probes and Lanczos quadrature depth is a specific recognized design choice in stochastic trace approximation; it is explicitly discussed in the 2023 depth/sample literature. The exact two-dimensional inverse-trace calculation discovers a parameterized reversal under equal matrix-vector cost, rather than merely refining a known table or restating unbiasedness. It provides an analyzable benchmark of when systematic one-node quadrature bias is worth the increase in sample count. The result expressly disclaims global black-box optimality and high-dimensional complexity, so its meaning is not inflated.
